clue.text: Violent infringement of rule reported in game

parts.note: violent behaviour is wild, out of control

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard spoken, so a soundalike is entered

parts.note: a foul is a breach of the rules in sport

explanation.surface: A rough breach of the rules is noted by the referee during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a sporting fixture, matching 'rule' and 'reported', but it means animals hunted for food. FOUL is said aloud as FOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks, geese and other wild birds shot for sport and the table count as game.

clue.text: Spinner greeting strange girl wearing toupee

indicators.note: the inner piece is wearing the outer one round it

parts.note: a toupee is a wig
hi is a casual greeting

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A rotating toy says hello to an odd girl in a hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a bowler or a storyteller but means a spinning toy; 'strange' jumbles the girl, and 'wearing' sets the greeting and jumbled letters under the toupee.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirligig is a spinning top or similar toy that spins.

clue.text: Clothes awaiting delivery

parts.note: delivery reads as a parcel in the post, but means a baby's birth, so garments made ready for a newborn

explanation.surface: Clothes ordered and waiting for the courier.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothing and linen prepared for a baby before it is born.

clue.text: Cold duck son originally tried to cook outside

indicators.note: outside means this piece goes round the others

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

indicators.note: originally picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Chilled duck, which the son first attempted to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird to cook, but is a zero, O. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosty means very cold, with a frost.

clue.text: Buttering up Democrat during revolution

indicators.note: during places one piece inside another

parts.note: wheeling is turning round, revolving

explanation.surface: Flattering a Democrat in the middle of an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a political uprising, matching 'Democrat', but means turning in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheedling means coaxing someone with flattery, buttering them up.

clue.text: Corporation involved in a peacekeeping organisation's fall

indicators.note: involved in places one piece within the letters of another

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, runs peacekeeping missions
corporation is an old joking word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A business gets tangled up in a peacekeeping body's collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a company, but it is the old slang for a large belly, TUM. 'fall' is the American word for the season.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English the fall is the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Stab a casual worker entered in races

indicators.note: entered in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: A temp is entered in the races for a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stab' looks violent but means a try, as in 'have a stab at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is an informal word for an attempt or try.

clue.text: It's used as tinder, all being well

definitions.meaning: rotten wood or dried fungus used to catch a spark
a phrase said to ward off bad luck, like knock on wood

explanation.surface: A lucky charm for lighting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchwood is tinder, and touch wood is said when hoping things go well.

clue.text: Simpleton serving alcohol in unsuitable vessels

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: mugs are wrong for serving spirits
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A fool serves spirits in mugs instead of glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is British slang for a fool, often meaning oneself, the dupe.

clue.text: Climber loses gold in tooth

indicators.note: loses means a piece is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: ivory is the material of tusks, the teeth of an elephant
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is short of a gold filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer but is a climbing plant. OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a familiar evergreen plant that climbs walls and trees.

clue.text: Excessively keyed up, like some pianos?

definitions.meaning: too tense or nervous, wound up too tightly
some pianos have their strings set crossing over each other

explanation.surface: A nervous person is compared to a tightly strung instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Overstrung means highly strung, nervy, and also names a piano whose strings cross diagonally.

clue.text: Freedom that comes by degrees?

definitions.meaning: scope or room to act as one chooses
position north or south of the equator is measured in degrees

explanation.surface: Liberty is something won gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means leeway or freedom, and is also a measure of position given in degrees.

clue.text: Start of musical show containing old yarn

indicators.note: containing means the earlier letters wrap round another piece
start of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Hair is a well-known rock musical

explanation.surface: The opening of a stage musical includes an old story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale, matching 'show', but means spun fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is yarn spun from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Energetic person disheartens one about to die

indicators.note: disheartens means the middle letter, the heart, is removed

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed or beyond help

explanation.surface: A lively type discourages someone near death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartens' reads as discourages; here it takes the heart (middle letter N) out of GONER.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is informal for a lively, energetic person who gets things done.

clue.text: Send away curate? It's unusual

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Should a curate be dismissed? It's not common.
explanation.walkthrough: Rusticating is used at British universities, sending a student down for a term.
explanation.definitionFit: To rusticate is to send someone off to the country, or suspend a student from university.

clue.text: It may prevent drifters being on the rocks

definitions.text: It may prevent drifters being on the rocks

parts.words: It may prevent drifters being on the rocks
parts.note: drifters reads as idle wanderers ruined and broke, but means fishing boats kept off reefs by a coastal beacon

explanation.surface: Something that keeps vagrants from destitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower with a warning lamp keeps ships, such as herring drifters, off rocks.

clue.text: Early advantage secured by the boss's floozie

parts.note: the head is the boss, so belonging to the head
tart is an insulting word for a floozie

explanation.surface: The boss's girlfriend secures an early lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given or taken at the beginning of a race.

clue.text: Possibly Pearly King's aim during festival season

definitions.note: Pearly Kings are Cockney charity figures in button suits, so one may be from London's East End; the 's means is

indicators.note: during places one piece inside another

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival season
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A Pearly King's goal for the holiday period.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possession but is 'is'; Pearly Kings and Queens are Cockney charity figures in suits sewn with pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pearly King is a traditional Cockney figure, so likely someone from London's East End.

clue.text: Scot making pathetic gag in Wales

indicators.note: pathetic, feeble and badly made, signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Scotsman tells a weak joke while in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link; the letters of GAG IN WALES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Glaswegian, someone from Glasgow, is one kind of Scot.

clue.text: Course two girls fail to finish

indicators.note: fail, read with to finish, says the first girl's word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl, and Agnes a girl's name

indicators.note: to finish, shared with fail, says the second girl's name also loses its final letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl, and Agnes a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two girls who drop out of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a race, but is a dish in a meal. 'fail to finish' acts on both girls: LASS and AGNES each lose their last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a pasta dish served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Coming out, I missed an American poet

indicators.note: missed means this letter is left out

parts.note: emersion is the act of emerging, coming out

explanation.surface: At a debut, I failed to see a US poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a 19th-century American poet and essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American poet and essayist.

clue.text: A Welshman's platform

definitions.meaning: Dai is the stock Welsh man's name in crosswords
a raised stage for speakers or guests of honour

explanation.surface: A man from Wales owns a raised stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The two readings are spelt alike once the apostrophe is dropped: Dai, short for David, is the typical Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform, and the letters also spell Dai's, belonging to a Welshman.

clue.text: Argue the point in relation to pouring the tea?

definitions.text: Argue the point in relation to pouring the tea?

parts.words: Argue the point in relation to pouring the tea?
parts.note: the phrase argue the point uses exactly the letters of pouring the tea, rearranged

explanation.surface: A quarrel about who should be mother at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase made by rearranging the letters of another phrase is the wordplay term described.

clue.text: Screen mystery

definitions.meaning: to sift gravel or soil through a coarse sieve

explanation.surface: A display that is a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve, and also a puzzling question or enigma.

clue.text: A stiffener put in second trial

indicators.note: put in signals one piece being placed inside another

parts.note: size is a gluey wash used to stiffen paper or cloth

explanation.surface: A support is added in the second attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' reads as a test, but means a court case. The assizes were periodic county courts in England and Wales until 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a session of a travelling court at which cases were tried.

clue.text: Hook, initially, and how he lived his life

parts.note: as means in the way that, answering how
Captain Hook of Peter Pan lived as a pirate

explanation.surface: A summary of Captain Hook: his first letter and his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Hook's initial is H, and an aspirate is the breathed H sound; Captain Hook lived AS a PIRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the breathy h sound, so the letter starting the word Hook is one.

clue.text: Flowering plant some kids will grow later? It depends

definitions.meaning: a meadow wildflower with downy seed heads, also called Jack-go-to-bed-at-noon

definitions.text: some kids will grow later? It depends
definitions.meaning: young goats, kids, may later sprout beards, depending on breed and sex

explanation.surface: A plant name that describes the facial hair young goats might later develop.
explanation.definitionFit: Goatsbeard is the name of a meadow plant with yellow flowers and fluffy clocks.

clue.text: Travelled out East to get staff

indicators.note: out means the following letter is dropped

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone rode out east to collect employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, but is a stick or pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a stick or pole, which is a staff.

clue.text: Flower always displayed in tin

indicators.note: displayed in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ever means at all times

explanation.surface: A bloom kept on show in a tin can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, a thing that flows. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flows is a flower in crossword language, and the Severn is a river.
